hook: Waiting ten years to invest can cost you almost three hundred thousand dollars.

blocks.narration: Waiting ten years to invest can cost you almost three hundred thousand dollars. Here is the math nobody shows you in school.
blocks.visual: Close-up of a clay hourglass where gold coins pour through the neck instead of sand, slow push-in, warm studio light

blocks.narration: Two friends each invest two hundred dollars every month into the same simple stock index fund. Nothing fancy, no stock picking at all.
blocks.visual: Two clay friends side by side, each dropping one gold coin into their own glass jar at the same moment

blocks.narration: Maya starts at twenty-five. Jake decides to wait until thirty-five, because there is always a car payment or a trip first.
blocks.visual: Maya keeps dropping coins while Jake lounges on a small clay couch holding a tiny toy car, his jar empty

blocks.narration: We will assume a seven percent average yearly return. Real markets bounce around, but long-run averages have looked roughly like this.
blocks.visual: A clay line chart rises in a jagged zigzag that trends steadily upward across a navy backdrop

blocks.narration: By sixty-five, Maya has about five hundred twenty-five thousand dollars. Jake, investing the exact same amount each month, has about two hundred forty-four thousand.
blocks.visual: Low-angle shot of two gold coin towers, Maya's soaring more than twice as tall as Jake's

blocks.narration: Here is the wild part. Over her whole life, Maya only contributed about twenty-four thousand dollars more than Jake did.
blocks.visual: A small extra stack of coins beside Maya glows softly while the towers loom behind it

blocks.narration: The difference is time. Every dollar invested early has more years to earn returns, and then those returns earn returns.
blocks.visual: A single gold coin splits into two, then four, then eight, multiplying across the frame

blocks.narration: You cannot buy back years, but you can start small today. Save this and share it with someone who keeps saying next year.
blocks.visual: Maya turns to camera holding out one gold coin as a tiny green leaf sprouts from it, golden sparkles

captions.hook_line: Same $200 a month. Ten years apart. A $281,000 difference 📈
captions.body: $200 a month at a hypothetical 7% average annual return, compounded monthly, until 65: about $525k if you start at 25, about $244k if you start at 35. The early starter puts in only $24k more.
